title: Circles
notes: A line and a circle can relate in 3 ways: non-intersecting (no common point), secant (2 common points), tangent (exactly 1 common point).
A tangent is really a secant in the limit -- when the two intersection points merge into one.
Theorem 10.1: The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. This is THE core fact of the chapter -- almost every proof uses it.
Number of tangents from a point: 0 if the point is INSIDE the circle, exactly 1 if the point is ON the circle, exactly 2 if the point is OUTSIDE the circle.
Theorem 10.2 (very important): The lengths of the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.

Standard proof toolkit for this chapter: right-angle at point of contact (radius perp tangent) + Pythagoras theorem + equal-tangent-lengths property. Most 'prove that...' questions combine these three.

formulas.name: Tangent length from external point
formulas.formula: PT = root(OP^2 - r^2)  [O=centre, r=radius, P=external point]
formulas.use: Direct application of Pythagoras since angle OTP = 90.

formulas.name: Equal tangents property
formulas.formula: PT1 = PT2 for two tangents from the same external point P
formulas.use: Used to prove side-sum relations in circumscribed quadrilaterals (AB+CD=AD+BC).

examples.question: Why must the point Q (other than P) on a tangent line always lie outside the circle?
examples.solution: If Q were inside or on the circle, the line would cross the circle at a second point, making it a secant, not a tangent (which by definition meets the circle at exactly one point).

exercises.question: How many tangents can a circle have?
exercises.answer: Infinitely many (one at every point on the circle)

exercises.question: Fill blanks: (i) A tangent intersects a circle in ___ point(s). (ii) A line intersecting a circle in 2 points is a ___. (iii) A circle can have ___ parallel tangents at most. (iv) The common point of tangent and circle is called ___.
exercises.answer: (i) one (ii) secant (iii) two (iv) point of contact
